title: Extra reference to a Resource if held by a global variable (potential memory leak)
body: ### Tested versions v4.4.1.stable ### System information Godot v4.4.1.stable (49a5bc7b6) - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2070 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6094) - AMD Ryzen 7 2700X Eight-Core Processor (16 threads) ### Issue description I wanted to refactor my code by turning certain class Nodes into class Resources (since all they did was hold data) and I wanted to make sure that the reference count goes to zero since I can't forcibly free it from memory like I can a Node. As I was testing it seemed that there is an extra reference I couldn't find. By reproducing the problem in a separate project and slowly cutting down on what's happening I managed to narrow it down to a Global variable (a var in a singleton) counting as two references to the resource. The problem is that if I then put "null" into that variable I don't know what happens to that resource and whether it just stays there in memory, leading to a memory leak every time I need to free or change said global variable. I don't know if this is a regression or if it was always a thing or if it's proper behavior and I couldn't get anyone else to verify it so I'm opening an issue. Until this is resolved or better understood I'll move back to using Nodes even though it can potentially hurt performance a little since I can control freeing those nodes with more confidence unlike the references. It could be related to this maybe: [https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.4/classes/class_refcounted.html](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.4/classes/class_refcounted.html) ### Steps to reproduce Create one scene and three scripts: - Resource script: ```js class_name Model extends Resource ``` - Global script (singleton): ```js // the global reference name is 'State' extends Node var model: Model ``` - Main Scene script: ```js extends Node func _ready() -> void: State.model = Model.new() print(State.model.get_reference_count()) ``` You'll see that the output is 2, despite there being only a singe assignment. If you use a local variable it will only count as 1 reference. If you do both it will total to 2(?) (in my personal project it actually counts to 3 but in this repro it's 2). If you add this code to the _ready() function: ```js var model_test: Model model_test = Model.new() print(model_test.get_reference_count()) // result: 1 model_test = State.selected_model print(model_test.get_reference_count()) // result: 2 model_test = null print(State.selected_model.get_reference_count()) // result: 2 model_test = State.selected_model State.selected_model = null print(model_test.get_reference_count()) // result: 1 ``` The results seem inconsistent with expected behavior. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) N/A
